drg.description: Simple Pneumonia and Pleurisy without CC/MCC

timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity
Transthoracic echo: LVEF 57%, grade I diastolic dysfunction

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 70-year-old male admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.65, bnp 247, creatinine 0.69, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 217, sodium 139, wbc 6.8; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 81-84, map 89-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 118-124, spo2 97-98, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Furosemide 20 mg PO daily (home med); Transthoracic echo: LVEF 57%, grade I diastolic dysfunction
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.7, hemoglobin 13.1, platelets 215, sodium 138, wbc 6.7; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 79-83, map 88-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 117-123, spo2 97-98, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Furosemide 20 mg PO daily (home med)
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 70-year-old male, length of stay 2 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
